what: Braze provides software that sends messages to customers. A company connects its app and website data to Braze, which then decides who receives which push notification, email or in-app message and when, based on what each customer has done.
customers: Consumer-facing companies with large user bases and a mobile app: streaming services, food delivery, retail, gaming, banking and media.
money: Recurring fees based on the number of customer profiles and messages sent.
moat: Once a company’s messaging logic — every campaign, trigger and customer segment — is built inside Braze, migrating means rebuilding all of it while the business keeps running. The product also sits between the company’s data and its customers, which means it accumulates behavioural history that makes the targeting better over time.
risks: A trailing net loss of $113.0M on $834.2M of revenue — the company is still not profitable on reported earnings.
Thirteen analysts average a $47.54 target against a $46.24 price, essentially no upside, which signals caution.
Growth has decelerated, and revenue depends on customers’ own user growth and marketing budgets.
Salesforce and Adobe bundle similar capability into platforms customers already buy, which pressures standalone tools.
The shares trade at about 6.3 times sales and 62.1 times free cash flow, which assumes growth continues.
opportunities: Revenue has grown very fast, from $238.0M in 2022 to $738.2M in 2026, with trailing revenue of $834.2M.
Free cash flow of $84.6M shows the business now generates cash even while reporting losses.
Cash of $124.3M against $82.7M of debt is a comfortable position.
Messaging logic built inside the platform is genuinely expensive for a customer to rebuild elsewhere.
Revenue grows with customers’ user bases without new sales effort, which is efficient expansion.
watch: Net revenue retention and customer count above the larger spending tiers. Growth in this category comes mostly from existing customers sending more messages to more users.
view: Braze sells the machinery behind every push notification you have ever received from an app. That sounds slight and is not: deciding which of fifty million users should get which message at which moment, based on what each of them did in the app yesterday, is a real data and infrastructure problem, and companies that try to build it themselves generally regret it.

The stickiness is the strongest part of the case. A customer’s entire messaging operation — every campaign, every trigger, every segment definition, built up over years by a marketing team — lives inside Braze. Migrating means rebuilding all of it while continuing to run the business, which is why these platforms are rarely displaced once embedded. Revenue growing from $238 million to $834 million in four years reflects both new customers and existing ones sending more.

The problems are the usual two for a single-purpose software company. Salesforce and Adobe include comparable capability in platforms their customers already buy, which is a permanent pricing headwind at the lower end. And growth has slowed: revenue depends on customers’ own user growth and marketing budgets, both of which tightened. A trailing loss of $113 million against $85 million of free cash flow is the familiar software gap, where share-based compensation consumes the accounting profit while cash arrives.

What I find most telling is the analyst picture: thirteen of them averaging a target within 3% of the share price. Sell-side analysts reliably forecast upside, so a group this size seeing none usually means their models cannot support more. At 6.3 times sales for a business growing but decelerating, and 62 times free cash flow, the price requires the deceleration to stop. Net revenue retention is the single number that tells you whether existing customers are expanding, and in this category that is where almost all growth comes from.
bull: Embedded messaging logic keeps customers in place while their user bases grow, net retention stays above 110%, and the business converts decisively to profitability.
bear: Salesforce and Adobe bundles win the mid-market, growth keeps decelerating against marketing budget cuts, and a 6 times sales multiple on an unprofitable business contracts.
